descriptionChirho: Preposition marking the agent of a passive verb, indicating the person or force by whom an action is performed. The most frequent NT use of ὑπό (171 occurrences). Translated with agentive prepositions: Spanish 'por,' Arabic 'مِنْ/مِنَ,' Hindi 'द्वारा/से,' Korean '에 의해' (by means of), Swahili 'na' (by). This governs the genitive case and functions as the primary passive agent marker in Koine Greek, equivalent to English 'by' in passive constructions.

Preposition indicating spatial position beneath or below something, or metaphorical subjection to authority, law, sin, or a condition. Rendered with locative/spatial terms: Spanish 'bajo,' Arabic 'تَحتَ/تَحْتَ,' Hindi 'नीचे,' Korean '아래에' (below/beneath), Swahili 'chini ya' (under/beneath). Governs the accusative case and encompasses both literal spatial meaning (under a bushel, under a fig tree) and figurative subjection (under the law, under sin, under a curse).

Rare prepositional use indicating temporal proximity or spatial nearness, rendered 'at' or 'near' rather than 'by' (agent) or 'under' (spatial). Distinguished by multilingual translations: English 'at,' Spanish 'hacia' (toward), Hindi 'मन्दिर में' (in the temple), Arabic 'عِنْدَ' (at/near), Swahili 'karibu na' (near to). This marginal sense appears in contexts where neither agentive nor strictly spatial-beneath readings apply, suggesting proximity or circumstantial location.
